nodes.title: Entry person = true and entry complaint ≠ true and entry chase …?
nodes.comment: ---- Why the call came here: entry markers from the supervisor ---------------------------- One marker says, as a typed value, why the supervisor routed the caller here. The step that acts on a marker consumes it, so a later entry for another reason never finds a stale one. A marker is acted on only when it is the one marker that is true (CONTRACT section 1). Each gate below therefore asks for its own marker and for the other four not to be true. Two or more true at once are values that reached this agent without being passed for this entry: none of the gates passes, drop_markers puts all five back, and the entry is read as it was before markers existed (a reason code, or the triage on the conversation). A marker entry carries no reason code: one left from an earlier visit is dropped. A summary, a queue and a booking reference that arrive together with the marker are kept (start has already read them into entry_summary, route_queue and reference_note): the outbound agent can so pass a marker and keep all three. The marker narrows the triage to the needs it can mean; with no marker and no reason code the triage runs as before. E27, A03, Q01: the caller asked for a person, a manager, or a call back from a person.

nodes.title: Understand request
nodes.detail: The caller has just been passed to you. In this step you only work out what they need. From what they have already said, decide which ONE of these it is and store it in request_ty…
nodes.comment: A02: the need, a chase included, is recognised from the caller's first words. With an entry marker the choice is narrowed to the needs that marker can mean (triage_hint). E28: an upset caller is only recognised here; the step acknowledge_upset says the apology. Q03: the summary for the person is written here when the call is going to a person. The note that came with the call is shown to the model because callers who are passed on without a reason code (a call made by the outbound agent, or a call to the number it calls out from) arrive with a summary and it must not be lost. The step speaks only when it has to ask. Once the need is stored it ends with no text: the next step acknowledges, answers or connects, or a tool runs behind the hold line. With no marker a request that is none of the listed needs is never handed back (the call may have come from an agent's ON_ERROR, and handing it back could send it round again): it is stored as other_request and a person takes over. Limit: the caller is asked at most twice; the third unclear answer goes to a person.

nodes.title: Request type = safety emergency?
nodes.comment: Safety inside this leaf agent. It declares no hand-off to the safety agent (that would close a cycle). With the return tool the model hands a safety remark back and the supervisor routes it. Without it (the caller came through a specialist's one-way escape) an emergency takes the urgent road: the roadside queue at once, no callback offer. A milder concern goes first in the summary and the caller carries on to a person.

nodes.title: Request type = pending?
nodes.comment: The need was never stored (the triage was left through a new entry that could no longer be taken from the top): a person takes over, with the reason code not_understood.

nodes.title: Entry summary known or triage hint known?
nodes.comment: With a note from the agent that passed the call (the outbound agent), a person simply takes the request over. The same when a marker came with the call (the triage note is set): the caller was routed here on purpose and wants something that could not be handed back. With nothing at all, an agent's ON_ERROR passed the call here.

nodes.title: System trouble entry
nodes.detail: I'm sorry, I'm having trouble with that just now.
nodes.say: I'm sorry, I'm having trouble with that just now.
nodes.comment: No marker, no reason code, no note, and nothing in the conversation that asks for a person: system trouble. The caller hears that once, then takes the road to a person. It counts as the first failure of the visit, so a failure after it is not announced again.

nodes.title: (handover reason known and handover reason ≠ entry reason) or e…?
nodes.comment: A step that talks to the caller ended because something changed. When a new entry has arrived in the meantime (this agent keeps its place when it hands a request back, and the caller may come back through the supervisor or through a specialist that needs a person), the entry is taken from the top so that what came with it is used as it came. Otherwise the caller changed their mind and the routing starts again.

nodes.title: Reroute count < 3?
nodes.comment: The caller changed their mind part-way through a step: start the routing again for the new need. A third change of mind in one visit goes straight to a person, so this cannot loop.

nodes.title: Transfer started = true?
nodes.comment: ---- Failures --------------------------------------------------------------------------- A tool did not answer after its one retry, a model call failed (ON_ERROR) or a constraint stopped a tool: say so briefly (the shared line, which promises nothing), then a person helps. A second failure in the same visit takes the short road below, which makes no model call and no tool call, so it cannot loop. The trouble line is said once in a visit: the second failure goes to the connecting line without it. A failure that arrives after the live hand-over was started (connect_person) can only be the hand-over itself. Every road below ends in connect_person again, so without this first check a transfer that cannot be made would be tried again and again, the connecting line said each time. It is tried once: the caller is told, and the flow ends on the closing question (transfer_not_made), as the safety agent and the front desk do in the same case.

nodes.comment: ---- Leaving without a transfer --------------------------------------------------------- The supervisor adds nothing after this agent returns. Every path that finishes a task and leaves the caller on the line (callback arranged, declined or not arranged, complaint raised, chase recorded, do not call recorded, and the advisor line of the demonstration) therefore ends here, with the shared line in the caller's language. Paths whose last line is already a question (a returned missed call) and the demo close line, which ends the call, go straight to finish. Like finish, the step drops the copies of the hand-over fields before it completes. spoken_line is not touched here: it has just been said, and start empties it at the next visit.
